title: A Single-Inductor-Based High-Voltage Transmit Beamformer for Wearable Ultrasound Devices Achieving 88% fCV2 Power Reduction
problem: Wearable ultrasound transducer arrays for vagus nerve stimulation suffer from excessive power loss from charging/discharging transducer capacitance (fCV² loss); prior resonant pulsers require multiple off-chip inductors, incompatible with miniaturized form factors.
motivation: Low-power wearable ultrasound therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy requires on-chip beamforming with energy-efficient transmit circuits; eliminating external inductors is critical for device miniaturization.
method: A single-inductor resonant transmit beamformer architecture pulses groups of transducer elements at different phases from a shared inductor, enabling energy recycling across the array while avoiding the complex body-diode losses of prior approaches.
key_novelty: Single-inductor architecture enabling efficient TX beamforming through phase-shifted pulsing of element groups, eliminating multiple off-chip inductors while maintaining resonant energy recycling.
contributions: Single-inductor topology replaces multiple off-chip inductors for compact wearable integration
Phase-shifted element group pulsing enables beamforming without additional energy loss
Resonant energy recycling avoiding body-diode conduction losses
Achieves 88% reduction in fCV² power loss vs. conventional class-D pulser

metrics.power_reduction: 88% fCV² loss reduction vs. class-D pulser

limitations: Specific acoustic pressure, beamforming resolution, and wearable device dimensions not specified.
primary_theme: Single-inductor resonant TX beamformer for wearable ultrasound therapy
